page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 2 vCPUs and 2 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or a dedicated GPU, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that leans toward the lower end of the spectrum, reflecting its shared CPU allocation. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the server in the bottom 10% category. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core performance, software compilation, and image processing benchmarks fall into the weak bottom 25% tier. However, the server demonstrates average middle 50% performance in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core scores. Memory bandwidth write tests also achieve average tier results, whereas read-only memory bandwidth remains weak.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU resource model, which limits its suitability for compute-intensive tasks, as evidenced by poor static web serving throughput and weak database operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a budget-friendly profile for workloads requiring a relatively large memory footprint of 16 GB without demanding sustained high-performance compute. It is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive tasks, basic background processing, development environments, or non-critical services that can tolerate shared CPU resource contention.
